gaps: Original uses `--$m` comment prefix (PML1 legacy style) for file path header; benchmark normalizes to `$*` (PML2 recommended). Both are valid, but `--$m` pattern is not explicitly documented in KB as a macro header convention.

Pattern `PML RELOAD OBJECT <name>` used to reload a previously-defined object before instantiation. Not found as a dedicated KB entry. Covered implicitly by macro/object lifecycle but not explicitly documented.

User-defined object `TAGMANAGEMENTTMP` with method `alarmsDataUpdate()` is external to KB. This is expected for customer-specific objects, but the pattern of `PML RELOAD OBJECT` followed by instantiation is a common idiom worth documenting.

newEntriesNeeded.title: PML RELOAD OBJECT command
newEntriesNeeded.principle: Reload a previously-defined PML object before creating instances to ensure the latest code is loaded.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Use `PML RELOAD OBJECT <name>` before `!var = object <name>()` when the object may have been updated since the session started.
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
PML RELOAD OBJECT TAGMANAGEMENTTMP
!tagMgmt = object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP()
!tagMgmt.alarmsDataUpdate()
pitfalls: RELOAD only works for objects previously defined in the current session (via .pmlobj file loaded earlier).
RELOAD does not work for system objects.
If the object has been modified externally, RELOAD is necessary to pick up changes without restarting AVEVA.

newEntriesNeeded.title: PML macro file header comment patterns
newEntriesNeeded.principle: Macros use comment headers to record source path and metadata. PML1 uses `--$m` with path; PML2 recommends `$*` comments.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Prefer `$*` for inline-safe comments. Use `--$m "path"` in legacy macros for path tracking.
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
$* Factory benchmark generated from semantic source summary only for mac_01
$* Source path: docs/codebase/macros/alarm_refresh.pmlmac

PML RELOAD OBJECT TAGMANAGEMENTTMP
pitfalls: `--$m` is a PML1 legacy pattern; `$*` is preferred in new code.
Path comments in `--$m` format may contain OneDrive/cloud-sync paths that break in production environments.
Do not copy absolute OneDrive paths into shared benchmarks.
